rules.title: Massachusetts rent control ballot initiative struck by SJC
rules.requirement: A proposed statewide ballot question limiting annual rent increases was blocked by the Supreme Judicial Court in June 2026 because of its religious-use exemption, so it will not go before voters in November 2026. No new rent cap results from it.
rules.quoted_span: The state’s Supreme Judicial Court ruled a ballot question seeking to bring rent control back to Massachusetts cannot go forward this November, because it includes a religious exemption.
rules.key_value: annual rent increase limit proposal; struck from 2026 ballot

no_rule_findings.finding: The proposed rent control ballot question was struck by the SJC, and no compromise legislation passed before July 1, so no statewide rent increase cap is created. The document does not itself mention the G.L. c.40P bar.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The ruling ends what promised to be one of the most expensive ballot initiative showdowns this year.

parsed.doc_summary: WBUR, 23 June 2026: the Massachusetts SJC struck the rent control ballot question from the November 2026 ballot because of its religious-use exemption. The article describes it as a failed measure, so I recorded it as one and added a no-rule finding.
